summary: Created Domain layer with 7 entities (Meeting, Session, Transcript, UtteranceEntity, SpeakerEntity, Note, AudioSegment), 5 ID types (MeetingID, SessionID, SpeakerID, TranscriptID, BackendID), 5 error types (TranscriptionError, StorageError, ValidationError, NetworkError, AudioError), all Sendable-safe with 100% conformance to Equatable, Hashable, Codable, and Sendable protocols
properties_addressed: SAFETY-004: Domain entities never expose mutable references
SAFETY-005: All domain types are Sendable-safe for Swift 6.2
INVARIANT-006: ID types prevent accidental mixing of different ID kinds
INVARIANT-007: All entities are immutable value types
INVARIANT-008: Zero external dependencies in Domain layer

decisions.description: Named Utterance entity as UtteranceEntity to avoid conflict with existing Utterance.swift in Domain folder
decisions.rationale: The existing Utterance.swift contains legacy code with Speaker enum that conflicts with the new 3-tier architecture design. Creating UtteranceEntity allows coexistence during migration period.

decisions.description: Named Speaker entity as SpeakerEntity to avoid conflict with existing Speaker enum in Utterance.swift
decisions.rationale: The existing Speaker enum is a simple case-based enum (.you, .them, .remote). SpeakerEntity is a proper domain entity with UUID-based identity for the new architecture.

decisions.description: Used Swift Duration type for time-based properties instead of TimeInterval
decisions.rationale: Duration provides better type safety and is the modern Swift way to represent time intervals, especially for Sendable conformance.

decisions.description: Implemented all entities as immutable structs with copy-on-write semantics via immutability
decisions.rationale: All update operations return new instances, preserving value semantics and ensuring thread-safety without locks.

decisions.description: Added UtteranceID and AudioSegmentID to the ID types collection
decisions.rationale: These IDs are necessary for the full domain model even though not explicitly listed in the task deliverables.
